question: True or false: in Britain, most people killed on the roads die in crashes where no driver was over the drink-drive limit?
answer: True. Crashes involving a driver over the limit account for roughly one road death in six in Great Britain. That does not make sober driving the danger: far more journeys are sober, so they supply most deaths even though each drunk mile is far riskier. Compare deaths per mile instead.
move: Divide by how common something is before calling it the main danger.
ask: When I hear most accidents happen somewhere, do I ask how much time people spend there?
trap: False, because drink-driving is famously the big killer on roads.
source: UK Department for Transport, road casualty statistics
reference: Department for Transport, Reported Road Casualties in Great Britain: Estimates for Accidents Involving Illegal Alcohol Levels, 2022
